definitions.gloss: utility knife; box cutter; craft knife
definitions.explanation: A retractable-blade cutting tool with snap-off segments. Extremely common in Japanese offices, schools, and households.

examples.japanese: カッターナイフで{段|だん}ボールを{切|き}った。
examples.english: I cut the cardboard with a utility knife.

examples.japanese: カッターナイフの{刃|は}を{新|あたら}しくした。
examples.english: I replaced the blade on the utility knife.

examples.japanese: {工作|こうさく}の{授業|じゅぎょう}でカッターナイフを{使|つか}うときは、{先生|せんせい}の{指示|しじ}に{従|したが}ってください。
examples.english: When using a utility knife in craft class, please follow the teacher's instructions.

notes:
A Japanese-English compound (wasei-eigo) combining "cutter" and "knife." In English this tool is typically called a utility knife, box cutter, or craft knife. In Japan, カッターナイフ (or simply カッター) is a standard school and office supply found in virtually every stationery shop.

The snap-off blade design was invented by the Japanese company OLFA in 1956 and became a global standard.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- カッターナイフの{刃|は}: utility knife blade
- カッターナイフで{切|き}る: to cut with a utility knife
- カッターナイフを{使|つか}う: to use a utility knife
- {替|か}え{刃|は}: replacement blade

SIMILAR WORDS:
- カッター: cutter — the everyday short form; same tool
- はさみ: scissors — for cutting paper and fabric with two blades
- ナイフ: knife — general term for any knife
